located_point.method: Published starting point (Abhayan et al. 2025 via the site index) checked on the composite: the village of Kanmer lies immediately south and a dark patch about 100 m across lies at the point, beside a bright modern road; no rectangle matching the 110 by 118 m fort of the plan could be outlined, so the point is the site index's coordinate rather than an independently located mound.

sources.imagery_result: no lines: the fort, which the plan draws turned about 30 degrees from its arrow, does not appear as a rectangle at 10 m; the only straight edges near the point are a modern road and field boundaries

sources.citation: J. S. Kharakwal, Y. S. Rawat, T. Osada, L. C. Patel, Hanmukh Seth, Rajesh Meena, S. Meena, K. P. Singh and A. Hussain 2011. Kanmer: A Multicultural Site in Kachchh, Gujarat, India. In Takao Uno (ed.), Changing Perceptions of Japan in South Asia in the New Asian Era, pp. 355-376. Kyoto: International Research Center for Japanese Studies
sources.figure: Fig. 5 Plan of Kanmer fort of Harappans
sources.north_evidence: Outlined arrow with a hatched arrowhead above the letter 'N', upper left; no stated meaning.
sources.scale_note: No scale bar. The plan is drawn on graph paper with a lettered and numbered excavation grid and the statement 'SCALE = 2CM=5M'. We took each lettered square as 5 m and calibrated on the outer ticks of the 30 squares K to NN; the fort sides then measure about 110 and 118 m.

line_files.locator: Kharakwal et al. 2011 PDF page 6, printed page 360, Fig. 5; render p01-kharakwal-fig5-250dpi.png (PDF region 65 232 445 625 pt, 250 dpi); picks picks/kanmer/plan-kanmer01-picks.json; fits by scripts-G/measure_each.py

notes: Plan only. The plan draws the excavation grid square to the page and to its arrow, and the fort walls turned about 30 degrees anticlockwise of both, so the folded deviations lie near -30 degrees, close to the folding limit; a fort turned the other way by 60 degrees would fold to the same values. The short south-west wall segment (theta -24.9) was split from the outer-fort system to keep the 6 degree window. The page text above the figure makes a qualitative statement about house alignment relative to the fort wall; it was not used.
